explanation: Retrospective detector of personal-life and testimony phrases in prose about people: it peaks on the completing word of (a) life-event and life-writing words (married, born, autobi-ography, memoir, childhood), (b) where someone stays or belongs after 'at'/possessive (at home, at school, his friend's/parents' house, at the hotel/office + 'all week/day'), (c) speech acts by people ('say/said/saying' after a quantified-people subject like '21 per cent', 'Half of the students', '40 percent of voters', or after 'to/would/might' with a human subject; 'told' with a human subject), and (d) 'not' right after 'to'/'for' in a person's instruction or promise ('asked her to not', 'apologized for not'); 'interview' is a sense-blind exception that fires in every context, even 'The interview module parses...'. It stays near zero (<0.25 of max) when the same frames are about machines, code, data or science ('The script told it to not', 'The servers stayed at the data center all week', 'The variable is stored at the home address', 'The log entries say', '40 percent of the samples', 'Set the married flag'), and also for 'I'-subject or bare-plural 'say' ('I would say', 'I can't say', 'Experts say', 'Users say'), 'went home', 'It is not', 'not to', and a house/home with only an article or as a modifier ('The old house on the hill', 'The home directory', 'Click the home button').
